slides.0.title: Regulations and labels
slides.0.subtitle: The layers of AOC, IGP and Vin de France
slides.1.title: Three tiers
slides.1.highlights.0.title: AOP / AOC
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The strictest tier, fixing varieties, yields and styles; each South-West AOC was granted at a different time
slides.1.highlights.1.title: IGP
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Wine With Seth: IGP is the second tier between AOP and Vin de France; under EU Regulation 607/2009, all Vin de Pays were renamed IGP on 1 August 2009
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Vin de France
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The bottom tier, with no regional claim; Wine With Seth counts 75 IGPs in France (6 regional, 28 departmental, 41 small zones)
slides.1.content: The same estate may make both AOC and IGP wines.
slides.2.title: Examples of AOC rules
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Cahors and Madiran
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Cahors: at least 70% Malbec, red only; Madiran: Tannat at least 60% of each estate's vineyard, red only (Wine With Seth, Wikipedia)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Jurançon sugar thresholds
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Jurançon Sec at most 4 g/L residual sugar; sweet at least 40 g/L; Vendanges Tardives at least 55 g/L (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Gaillac's styles
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Gaillac Doux has at least 70 g/L; Primeur is pure Gamay released on the third Thursday of November; Méthode Gaillacoise uses Mauzac only (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.content: A single AOC can contain dry, sweet and sparkling styles.
slides.3.title: IGPs and volume wines
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Côtes de Gascogne
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Wine With Seth: about 12,000 ha centred on the Gers, roughly 85% white (Colombard, Ugni Blanc, Gros Manseng, Sauvignon Blanc)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Specification details
slides.3.highlights.1.content: INAO draft specification: recognised as a vin de pays by decree on 25 January 1982; yield limit 120 hL/ha; minimum 9.0% abv without enrichment
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Comté Tolosan
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Wine With Seth: it covers the South-West excluding Gascony; compare Pays d'Oc at about 120,000 ha with 58 permitted varieties
slides.3.content: IGP gives estates more freedom in varieties and style than AOC.
slides.4.title: Labels and related products
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Varietal labelling
slides.4.highlights.0.content: To name a variety on an IGP label, it must make up at least 85% (Wine With Seth)
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Appellation names first
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Wikipedia: wines are rarely sold as Vins du Sud-Ouest; smaller areas and individual appellations use their own names
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Armagnac and Floc
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Armagnac is a brandy made in Gascony; some grape must is mixed with Armagnac to make the mistelle Floc de Gascogne (Wikipedia)
slides.4.content: Level 2 looks at each area's actual rules.
